metrics.prompt:
Repaint the attached grey block-out as ONE finished building sprite for a pastoral isometric railway game.

Style: that of the attached style board. Crisp pixel-art-inspired clustered shading, broad readable masses, three or four shades per material, restrained detail, a strong silhouette. The palette family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B, slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest, lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest.

Camera: keep the block-out's camera exactly. Orthographic 2:1 isometric, ground edges two pixels across for each pixel down, vertical edges vertical, no perspective. Do not rotate or tilt the view. The foot of the lower-left wall runs parallel to the plinth's lower-left edge and the foot of the lower-right wall parallel to its lower-right edge: both walls equally steep, neither flatter than the block-out's. Do not turn the building towards the viewer: the lower-right wall is seen as much from the side as the lower-left wall. Show the whole building with a clear margin all round: nothing touches the edge of the picture.

Footprint: the grey plinth is the building's footprint. The building stands on it and fills it: its outer walls rise from the plinth's edges, and at ground level nothing reaches outside the plinth. Keep the foot of the two visible walls plain and straight from corner to corner, so that it shows where the building stands: no bushes, crates, steps or loose objects in front of it. Above the ground the shape is free: roofs, towers, chimneys and machinery may differ from the block and may overhang a little. The dark openings in the block-out show where the front door, or a depot's train portals, are; keep them in those walls.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building surfaces.

Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow, or loose objects standing apart from the building.

Building: Narrow Depot. A small single-track engine shed for narrow-gauge trains, which run through it: a narrow hall with one portal in each end wall.

Age: Steam (model 1 of 6 for this building). Steam age, the first railway: small and rural. Timber framing, cream limestone, warm brick, slate roofs, cast-iron posts, evergreen-painted woodwork, a chimney where it makes sense.

This building in this age: A timber plank shed on a cream stone footing with a slate roof and one round-arched portal per end.

Keep in every age: one train portal in each end wall, clearly smaller than a main-line depot. The portal is a doorway into the hall, and the inside of the hall shows through it: inside the doorway paint the hall's inner wall, in shadow. Only the floor is left out: below that inner wall the ground inside the doorway, up to about a third of the doorway's height, and the ground before it stay unpainted and transparent, so that the game's rails show there. Do not make the whole doorway transparent, and paint no floor, threshold, apron or rails. Also keep: a small crew door in the front long wall.

Front: the long wall with the crew door; the track runs through the hall parallel to it.

View r0: The front faces the lower left. The lower-left wall is the FRONT; the lower-right wall is the building's right-hand side (to the right of someone standing outside and facing the front). The train portal is in the LOWER-RIGHT wall, where the block-out has its large dark opening.

References: the first is the style board. The second is the main-line depot of the same age, laid onto its own footprint: match its materials and details. This shed is smaller, with one portal in each end wall. The last reference is a mood board for this age: take only its materials and mood from it, never its perspective, its landscape or its trains.

CORE REVIEW 2 OVERRIDE: any earlier printed sentence about leaving a transparent doorway/floor or no floor is superseded. Paint the hall interior, dark FLOOR and SILL FULLY OPAQUE to the foot line, exactly like the first input; NO ALPHA NOTCH anywhere inside the portal. Background only is transparent.

THE SHED: a narrow single-track hall of timber planks and brick on a cream stone footing, a slate gable roof with a smoke vent along the ridge, ONE round-arched portal in each end wall with evergreen timber doors folded open (inside each doorway the hall's inner wall in shadow and the hall's floor: an opaque dark floor and sill, as the lit render shows them, running out to the foot line of the end wall; nothing in the doorway is transparent, and nothing is painted in front of the foot line), a small crew door and two small windows in the front long wall. Narrower and smaller than the depot: the portal is 0.44 tile wide and 24 game px high. The palette family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B, slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest, lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest. Nothing at or above cursor white #ECE4D0 and nothing as strong as selection amber #E8AA48.

r0, the front: the long lower-left wall is the FRONT, with the crew door and the two small windows; the lower-right wall is the end wall with its portal.

The first picture is not a painting but a plain 3D blockout of the narrow depot at the game's exact camera: keep its shape, outline, camera and layout exactly as they are (every roof, wall, portal, door, window and vent where the blockout has it, nothing added outside its outline or taken out of it) and paint EVERY surface of it in the game's painted style, from the materials and details of the depot picture. Paint no plinth, ground or shadow; the foot of the walls starts at the blockout's corners. Do not rotate, tilt, resize, shift or reshape the building. The doorway of each end wall is solid in the blockout: paint the hall's inner wall in shadow and its dark floor and sill as the blockout shows them, fully opaque, with the door leaves as they stand; no part of the doorway is transparent.

Output1024x1024 transparent RGBA. Input1 is the edit target, remaining inputs as listed reference roles. Preserve exact full-canvas location, original size, geometry, all parts, and empty margins of the blockout. The lower-left wall is lighter and lower-right darkest; no ground or shadow outside the foot line.
